School & learning

globe noun

a model of the earth

also terrestrial globe, school globe

modern

Traupman 29
Traupman 321

globus terrārum

a globe

A ball of the lands. Cicero calls the earth itself a globe: illum globum … quae terra dīcitur (Rep. 6.15), and gives globus as the Latin for σφαῖρα (N. D. 2.47).

Other words

  • sphaera, sphaerae f. — a sphere; a model globe, classically of the heavens

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Rep. 1.21–22; Cic. Tusc. 1.63 (Lewis & Short)

    Archimedes’ sphere, which showed the courses of the sun, the moon and the planets, was a sphaera (Cic. Rep. 1.21–22).

  • globus terrestris

    also used · modern · Andresian p. 11

Examples

  • Hominēs enim sunt hāc lēge generātī, quī tuērentur illum globum, quem in hōc templō medium vidēs, quae terra dīcitur

    For men were born on these terms, to look after that globe you see in the middle of this temple, which is called the earthCic. Rep. 6.15

  • Quaere in globō ubi sit Lūsitānia.

    Find Portugal on the globe.composed

See also map, world, geography, ball.
